## The defect

Bug 7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14 fixed the `Git version floor gate` step, which hard-failed every
change branched before its data file landed. The same class of defect is still live in
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` on OTHER gate steps that run a repo script with no
if-present guard.

The workflow's own "Definition-vs-tree skew guard (ticket ee2a)" note states the rule
verbatim: a gate step that runs a repo script must skip (with a log line) when the script is
absent from the checked-out tree. Gerrit's Verified lane takes the workflow DEFINITION from
the target branch but checks out the CHANGE'S tree, so a step added on main runs against
open changes whose base predates its script.

## Unguarded gate steps (swept from the parsed workflow YAML)

In `_build-and-test.yml`, which BOTH the Gerrit Verified lane and branch CI run:

| step | script | script first added |
|---|---|---|
| `comment-hygiene gate` | `scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` | 2026-08-03 |
| `Config-read gate` | `scripts/check_config_reads.py` | 2026-08-02 |
| `Verified-gate parity gate` | `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` | 2026-07-19 |
| `Env-var registry drift gate` | `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` | 2026-07-08 |
| `Docs-index completeness gate` | `scripts/check_docs_index.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `README quickstart golden-path gate` | `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `CLI-reference drift gate` | `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `MCP-reference drift gate` | `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` | 2026-07-11 |
| `server.json env-contract drift gate` | `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` | 2026-07-04 |

The two 2026-08-02/03 scripts are the LIVE exposure -- open changes branched before those
dates exist today. The older ones are the same latent class and should be guarded for
uniformity, so the next reader does not have to re-derive which are safe.

`gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `golden-path` job also checks out the Gerrit patchset and runs
`scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/probe_rebar.py` unguarded -- same class,
same lane.

## Confirmed empirically

Running each unguarded step's command in a directory without the script exits 2 with
`can't open file '.../scripts/<name>.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory` -- a hard CI
failure indistinguishable from a real gate violation, which is exactly what produced the
false Verified -1 in 7e90.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every gate step in `_build-and-test.yml` that runs a repo script carries the ee2a
      if-present guard, skipping with a log line naming the tree-skew cause.
- [x] The `golden-path` job in `gerrit-verify.yaml` is guarded the same way.
- [x] A genuine gate violation still fails when the script IS present -- no gate is weakened.
- [x] A test (mirroring `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py`) executes each guarded
      step against a tree lacking the script and asserts it exits 0 without an `::error::`.
- [x] Consider a structural guard: a check that FAILS when a step in the Verified lane runs a
      repo script without the if-present guard, so the convention stops depending on authors
      remembering the ee2a note.

## Provenance

Found by the Step 7 sibling sweep while fixing bug 7e90-233b-3ee9-4f14.
